name: k-age-presentation
question: Which age presentation on a `## Knowledge` provenance stamp actually keys a reader into staleness -- none, absolute date, relative age, a qualitative T-shirt label, or an explicit status/action line?

arms.none: (K7E-000-00003) -- control, no age information at all
arms.qualitative: (K7E-000-00003, 36d old — very old) -- T-shirt label from fixtures/presentation.json, omitted under 7d
arms.status: (K7E-000-00003, 36d old) plus a `Status: possibly superseded...` line on entries older than 30d

tasks.t1: update-conflict -- store holds an old (36d) and a new (2d) entry on the same subject; correct = states the new fact, stale_following = states the old fact, hedged = states/implies both or uses uncertainty language
tasks.t2: stale-alone -- store holds only an old fact (90d) plus unrelated filler; correct behavior is hedging (hedged), failure is a confident unqualified restatement of the old fact (asserted_unqualified)

readers.qwen: qwen3:4b via local ollama /api/generate (4B comparability floor)
readers.agy: Antigravity (agy) --model gemini-3.6-flash-low via the verified sh -c stdin wrapper

predictions.claim: qualitative and/or status beat none and absolute on T1 correct-rate
qualitative and/or status beat none and absolute on T2 hedge-rate

org.note: Not org/posthoc-class -- no r4t roster, no member, no dispatch process. The prompt is hand-built text mirroring apps/r4t/dispatch.py's prompt_sections shape and apps/r4t/knowledge.py's knowledge_section block format (imports KNOWLEDGE_HEADER/KNOWLEDGE_FRAMING directly so the shell never drifts from what ships). Same bespoke-driver precedent as k0-knowledge-inject, k-next-embeddings, and k4e-poisoning.
